what_its_for: Berotralstat is used to prevent attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in adults and children 12 years and older. HAE is a condition that causes sudden swelling in different parts of the body, such as the face, throat, stomach, hands, and feet. This medicine helps reduce how often these swelling attacks happen, but it does NOT treat an attack that has already started.
how_to_take: Take berotralstat by mouth once a day with food. Swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Always take it with a meal or snack to help reduce stomach upset.
dosing: The usual dose for adults and children 12 years and older is 150 mg (one capsule) taken by mouth once daily with food. Your doctor may lower your dose to 110 mg once daily if you have certain liver problems or if you are taking certain other medicines. Always follow your doctor's instructions exactly and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at your regular time. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store berotralstat capsules at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Protect from moisture. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it past the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking berotralstat with certain medicines without first talking to your doctor or pharmacist, as some medications can interact with it and raise or lower the amount of berotralstat in your blood. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take. Avoid starting new medicines without checking with your doctor first. This medicine is NOT for treating an active HAE attack — always have your rescue medicine available for breakthrough attacks.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: sudden or severe stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat; yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual tiredness (signs of liver problems); any new or worsening symptoms. Also contact your doctor if you feel the medicine is not preventing your HAE attacks as expected.
when_it_works: Berotralstat starts working gradually. Most people begin to see a reduction in the number of HAE attacks within the first month of treatment. The full benefit is usually seen after about 3 months of taking the medicine regularly every day. It is important to keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because stopping may cause your attacks to return.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The safety of berotralstat during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. Liver problems: If you have moderate or severe liver disease, your doctor may give you a lower dose or monitor you more closely. Kidney problems: No dose adjustment is usually needed for mild to moderate kidney disease, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues. Children: This medicine is approved for children 12 years and older at the same dose as adults. It has not been studied in children under 12.
